scene.label: Act 2, Scene 2
scene.title: SCENE II. Another Room in the palace

content.text: Enter the old Duchess of York with the two Children of Clarence.

lines.text: Good grandam, tell us, is our father dead?
lines.plainText: Good grandam tell us is our father dead

lines.text: No, boy.
lines.plainText: No boy

lines.text: Why do you weep so oft, and beat your breast,
lines.plainText: Why do you weep so oft and beat your breast

lines.text: And cry "O Clarence, my unhappy son"?
lines.plainText: And cry O Clarence my unhappy son

lines.text: Why do you look on us, and shake your head,
lines.plainText: Why do you look on us and shake your head

lines.text: And call us orphans, wretches, castaways,
lines.plainText: And call us orphans wretches castaways

lines.text: If that our noble father were alive?
lines.plainText: If that our noble father were alive

lines.text: My pretty cousins, you mistake me both.
lines.plainText: My pretty cousins you mistake me both

lines.text: I do lament the sickness of the King,
lines.plainText: I do lament the sickness of the King

lines.text: As loath to lose him, not your father's death.
lines.plainText: As loath to lose him not your father's death

lines.text: It were lost sorrow to wail one that's lost.
lines.plainText: It were lost sorrow to wail one that's lost

lines.text: Then you conclude, my grandam, he is dead.
lines.plainText: Then you conclude my grandam he is dead

lines.text: The King mine uncle is to blame for it.
lines.plainText: The King mine uncle is to blame for it

lines.text: God will revenge it, whom I will importune
lines.plainText: God will revenge it whom I will importune

lines.text: With earnest prayers all to that effect.
lines.plainText: With earnest prayers all to that effect

lines.text: And so will I.
lines.plainText: And so will I

lines.text: Peace, children, peace. The King doth love you well.
lines.plainText: Peace children peace The King doth love you well

lines.text: Incapable and shallow innocents,
lines.plainText: Incapable and shallow innocents

lines.text: You cannot guess who caused your father's death.
lines.plainText: You cannot guess who caused your father's death

lines.text: Grandam, we can, for my good uncle Gloucester
lines.plainText: Grandam we can for my good uncle Gloucester

lines.text: Told me, the King, provoked to it by the Queen,
lines.plainText: Told me the King provoked to it by the Queen

lines.text: Devised impeachments to imprison him;
lines.plainText: Devised impeachments to imprison him

lines.text: And when my uncle told me so, he wept,
lines.plainText: And when my uncle told me so he wept

lines.text: And pitied me, and kindly kissed my cheek;
lines.plainText: And pitied me and kindly kissed my cheek

lines.text: Bade me rely on him as on my father,
lines.plainText: Bade me rely on him as on my father

lines.text: And he would love me dearly as his child.
lines.plainText: And he would love me dearly as his child

lines.text: Ah, that deceit should steal such gentle shape,
lines.plainText: Ah that deceit should steal such gentle shape

lines.text: And with a virtuous visard hide deep vice!
lines.plainText: And with a virtuous visard hide deep vice

lines.text: He is my son, ay, and therein my shame;
lines.plainText: He is my son ay and therein my shame

lines.text: Yet from my dugs he drew not this deceit.
lines.plainText: Yet from my dugs he drew not this deceit

lines.text: Think you my uncle did dissemble, grandam?
lines.plainText: Think you my uncle did dissemble grandam

lines.text: Ay, boy.
lines.plainText: Ay boy

lines.text: I cannot think it. Hark, what noise is this?
lines.plainText: I cannot think it Hark what noise is this

content.text: Enter Queen Elizabeth with her hair about her ears, Rivers and Dorset after her.

lines.text: Ah, who shall hinder me to wail and weep,
lines.plainText: Ah who shall hinder me to wail and weep

lines.text: To chide my fortune, and torment myself?
lines.plainText: To chide my fortune and torment myself

lines.text: I'll join with black despair against my soul
lines.plainText: I'll join with black despair against my soul

lines.text: And to myself become an enemy.
lines.plainText: And to myself become an enemy

lines.text: What means this scene of rude impatience?
lines.plainText: What means this scene of rude impatience

lines.text: To make an act of tragic violence.
lines.plainText: To make an act of tragic violence

lines.text: Edward, my lord, thy son, our King, is dead.
lines.plainText: Edward my lord thy son our King is dead

lines.text: Why grow the branches when the root is gone?
lines.plainText: Why grow the branches when the root is gone

lines.text: Why wither not the leaves that want their sap?
lines.plainText: Why wither not the leaves that want their sap

lines.text: If you will live, lament; if die, be brief,
lines.plainText: If you will live lament if die be brief

lines.text: That our swift-winged souls may catch the King's
lines.plainText: That our swiftwinged souls may catch the King's

lines.text: Or, like obedient subjects, follow him
lines.plainText: Or like obedient subjects follow him

lines.text: To his new kingdom of ne'er-changing night.
lines.plainText: To his new kingdom of ne'erchanging night

lines.text: Ah, so much interest have I in thy sorrow
lines.plainText: Ah so much interest have I in thy sorrow

lines.text: As I had title in thy noble husband.
lines.plainText: As I had title in thy noble husband

lines.text: I have bewept a worthy husband's death,
lines.plainText: I have bewept a worthy husband's death

lines.text: And lived by looking on his images;
lines.plainText: And lived by looking on his images

lines.text: But now two mirrors of his princely semblance
lines.plainText: But now two mirrors of his princely semblance

lines.text: Are cracked in pieces by malignant death,
lines.plainText: Are cracked in pieces by malignant death

lines.text: And I, for comfort, have but one false glass,
lines.plainText: And I for comfort have but one false glass

lines.text: That grieves me when I see my shame in him.
lines.plainText: That grieves me when I see my shame in him

lines.text: Thou art a widow, yet thou art a mother,
lines.plainText: Thou art a widow yet thou art a mother

lines.text: And hast the comfort of thy children left;
lines.plainText: And hast the comfort of thy children left

lines.text: But death hath snatched my husband from mine arms
lines.plainText: But death hath snatched my husband from mine arms

lines.text: And plucked two crutches from my feeble hands,
lines.plainText: And plucked two crutches from my feeble hands

lines.text: Clarence and Edward. O, what cause have I,
lines.plainText: Clarence and Edward O what cause have I

lines.text: Thine being but a moiety of my moan,
lines.plainText: Thine being but a moiety of my moan

lines.text: To overgo thy woes and drown thy cries.
lines.plainText: To overgo thy woes and drown thy cries

lines.text: Ah, aunt, you wept not for our father's death.
lines.plainText: Ah aunt you wept not for our father's death

lines.text: How can we aid you with our kindred tears?
lines.plainText: How can we aid you with our kindred tears

lines.text: Our fatherless distress was left unmoaned.
lines.plainText: Our fatherless distress was left unmoaned

lines.text: Your widow-dolour likewise be unwept!
lines.plainText: Your widowdolour likewise be unwept

lines.text: Give me no help in lamentation.
lines.plainText: Give me no help in lamentation

lines.text: I am not barren to bring forth complaints.
lines.plainText: I am not barren to bring forth complaints

lines.text: All springs reduce their currents to mine eyes,
lines.plainText: All springs reduce their currents to mine eyes

lines.text: That I, being governed by the watery moon,
lines.plainText: That I being governed by the watery moon

lines.text: May send forth plenteous tears to drown the world.
lines.plainText: May send forth plenteous tears to drown the world

lines.text: Ah, for my husband, for my dear Lord Edward!
lines.plainText: Ah for my husband for my dear Lord Edward

lines.text: Ah for our father, for our dear Lord Clarence!
lines.plainText: Ah for our father for our dear Lord Clarence

lines.text: Alas for both, both mine, Edward and Clarence!
lines.plainText: Alas for both both mine Edward and Clarence

lines.text: What stay had I but Edward? And he's gone.
lines.plainText: What stay had I but Edward And he's gone

lines.text: What stay had we but Clarence? And he's gone.
lines.plainText: What stay had we but Clarence And he's gone

lines.text: What stays had I but they? And they are gone.
lines.plainText: What stays had I but they And they are gone

lines.text: Was never widow had so dear a loss.
lines.plainText: Was never widow had so dear a loss

lines.text: Were never orphans had so dear a loss.
lines.plainText: Were never orphans had so dear a loss

lines.text: Was never mother had so dear a loss.
lines.plainText: Was never mother had so dear a loss

lines.text: Alas, I am the mother of these griefs.
lines.plainText: Alas I am the mother of these griefs

lines.text: Their woes are parcelled, mine is general.
lines.plainText: Their woes are parcelled mine is general

lines.text: She for an Edward weeps, and so do I;
lines.plainText: She for an Edward weeps and so do I

lines.text: I for a Clarence weep, so doth not she;
lines.plainText: I for a Clarence weep so doth not she

lines.text: These babes for Clarence weep, and so do I;
lines.plainText: These babes for Clarence weep and so do I

lines.text: I for an Edward weep, so do not they.
lines.plainText: I for an Edward weep so do not they

lines.text: Alas, you three, on me, threefold distressed,
lines.plainText: Alas you three on me threefold distressed

lines.text: Pour all your tears. I am your sorrow's nurse,
lines.plainText: Pour all your tears I am your sorrow's nurse

lines.text: And I will pamper it with lamentation.
lines.plainText: And I will pamper it with lamentation

lines.text: Comfort, dear mother. God is much displeased
lines.plainText: Comfort dear mother God is much displeased

lines.text: That you take with unthankfulness His doing.
lines.plainText: That you take with unthankfulness His doing

lines.text: In common worldly things 'tis called ungrateful
lines.plainText: In common worldly things 'tis called ungrateful

lines.text: With dull unwillingness to repay a debt
lines.plainText: With dull unwillingness to repay a debt

lines.text: Which with a bounteous hand was kindly lent;
lines.plainText: Which with a bounteous hand was kindly lent

lines.text: Much more to be thus opposite with heaven,
lines.plainText: Much more to be thus opposite with heaven

lines.text: For it requires the royal debt it lent you.
lines.plainText: For it requires the royal debt it lent you

lines.text: Madam, bethink you, like a careful mother,
lines.plainText: Madam bethink you like a careful mother

lines.text: Of the young prince your son. Send straight for him;
lines.plainText: Of the young prince your son Send straight for him

lines.text: Let him be crowned; in him your comfort lives.
lines.plainText: Let him be crowned in him your comfort lives

lines.text: Drown desperate sorrow in dead Edward's grave,
lines.plainText: Drown desperate sorrow in dead Edward's grave

lines.text: And plant your joys in living Edward's throne.
lines.plainText: And plant your joys in living Edward's throne

content.text: Enter Richard, Buckingham, Stanley Earl of Derby, Hastings and Ratcliffe.

lines.text: Sister, have comfort. All of us have cause
lines.plainText: Sister have comfort All of us have cause

lines.text: To wail the dimming of our shining star,
lines.plainText: To wail the dimming of our shining star

lines.text: But none can help our harms by wailing them.
lines.plainText: But none can help our harms by wailing them

lines.text: Madam my mother, I do cry you mercy;
lines.plainText: Madam my mother I do cry you mercy

lines.text: I did not see your Grace. Humbly on my knee
lines.plainText: I did not see your Grace Humbly on my knee

lines.text: I crave your blessing.
lines.plainText: I crave your blessing

lines.text: God bless thee, and put meekness in thy breast,
lines.plainText: God bless thee and put meekness in thy breast

lines.text: Love, charity, obedience, and true duty.
lines.plainText: Love charity obedience and true duty

lines.text: Amen. [Aside.] And make me die a good old man!
lines.plainText: Amen Aside And make me die a good old man

lines.text: That is the butt end of a mother's blessing;
lines.plainText: That is the butt end of a mother's blessing

lines.text: I marvel that her Grace did leave it out.
lines.plainText: I marvel that her Grace did leave it out

lines.text: You cloudy princes and heart-sorrowing peers
lines.plainText: You cloudy princes and heartsorrowing peers

lines.text: That bear this heavy mutual load of moan,
lines.plainText: That bear this heavy mutual load of moan

lines.text: Now cheer each other in each other's love.
lines.plainText: Now cheer each other in each other's love

lines.text: Though we have spent our harvest of this king,
lines.plainText: Though we have spent our harvest of this king

lines.text: We are to reap the harvest of his son.
lines.plainText: We are to reap the harvest of his son

lines.text: The broken rancour of your high-swoll'n hates,
lines.plainText: The broken rancour of your highswoll'n hates

lines.text: But lately splintered, knit, and joined together,
lines.plainText: But lately splintered knit and joined together

lines.text: Must gently be preserved, cherished, and kept.
lines.plainText: Must gently be preserved cherished and kept

lines.text: Me seemeth good that with some little train,
lines.plainText: Me seemeth good that with some little train

lines.text: Forthwith from Ludlow the young Prince be fet
lines.plainText: Forthwith from Ludlow the young Prince be fet

lines.text: Hither to London, to be crowned our King.
lines.plainText: Hither to London to be crowned our King

lines.text: Why with some little train, my Lord of Buckingham?
lines.plainText: Why with some little train my Lord of Buckingham

lines.text: Marry, my lord, lest by a multitude
lines.plainText: Marry my lord lest by a multitude

lines.text: The new-healed wound of malice should break out,
lines.plainText: The newhealed wound of malice should break out

lines.text: Which would be so much the more dangerous
lines.plainText: Which would be so much the more dangerous

lines.text: By how much the estate is green and yet ungoverned.
lines.plainText: By how much the estate is green and yet ungoverned

lines.text: Where every horse bears his commanding rein
lines.plainText: Where every horse bears his commanding rein

lines.text: And may direct his course as please himself,
lines.plainText: And may direct his course as please himself

lines.text: As well the fear of harm as harm apparent,
lines.plainText: As well the fear of harm as harm apparent

lines.text: In my opinion, ought to be prevented.
lines.plainText: In my opinion ought to be prevented

lines.text: I hope the King made peace with all of us;
lines.plainText: I hope the King made peace with all of us

lines.text: And the compact is firm and true in me.
lines.plainText: And the compact is firm and true in me

lines.text: And so in me, and so, I think, in all.
lines.plainText: And so in me and so I think in all

lines.text: Yet since it is but green, it should be put
lines.plainText: Yet since it is but green it should be put

lines.text: To no apparent likelihood of breach,
lines.plainText: To no apparent likelihood of breach

lines.text: Which haply by much company might be urged.
lines.plainText: Which haply by much company might be urged

lines.text: Therefore I say with noble Buckingham
lines.plainText: Therefore I say with noble Buckingham

lines.text: That it is meet so few should fetch the Prince.
lines.plainText: That it is meet so few should fetch the Prince

lines.text: And so say I.
lines.plainText: And so say I

lines.text: Then be it so, and go we to determine
lines.plainText: Then be it so and go we to determine

lines.text: Who they shall be that straight shall post to Ludlow.
lines.plainText: Who they shall be that straight shall post to Ludlow

lines.text: Madam, and you, my sister, will you go
lines.plainText: Madam and you my sister will you go

lines.text: To give your censures in this business?
lines.plainText: To give your censures in this business

lines.text: My lord, whoever journeys to the Prince,
lines.plainText: My lord whoever journeys to the Prince

lines.text: For God's sake, let not us two stay at home.
lines.plainText: For God's sake let not us two stay at home

lines.text: For by the way I'll sort occasion,
lines.plainText: For by the way I'll sort occasion

lines.text: As index to the story we late talked of,
lines.plainText: As index to the story we late talked of

lines.text: To part the Queen's proud kindred from the Prince.
lines.plainText: To part the Queen's proud kindred from the Prince

lines.text: My other self, my counsel's consistory,
lines.plainText: My other self my counsel's consistory

lines.text: My oracle, my prophet, my dear cousin,
lines.plainText: My oracle my prophet my dear cousin

lines.text: I, as a child, will go by thy direction.
lines.plainText: I as a child will go by thy direction

lines.text: Toward Ludlow then, for we'll not stay behind.
lines.plainText: Toward Ludlow then for we'll not stay behind
